To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a machine learning based method to reliably detect subjects who have spent enough time within 2m of each other to be at risk for being infected by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, and that we have demonstrated that our approach can be successfully applied to data from a real world setting, namely the SwissCovid app.

our machine learning approach can be used to detect subjects that are at high risk of being infected by a SARS CoV2 carrier, and that this approach is more reliable than the one based on the current standard of 15 minutes proximity.
we can reliably detect subjects at risk of being exposed to the SARS CoV2 virus based on Bluetooth measurements, with a precision of 95.6% and recall of 92.4% (area under the curve 0.95).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) How to estimate the transmission risk of an individual given a sequence of Bluetooth low energy measurements?

(a) the design of a machine learning based framework to detect subjects that have been in close proximity to a COVID 19 positive subject, (b) the development of a novel metric for the quantification of the risk of infection, and (c) the evaluation of the performance of our framework using data from the COVID 19 outbreak in Iceland.
the following questions: 1) What are the characteristics of Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) measurements that are indicative of close proximity between individuals?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach has the potential to reliably detect subjects who have spent enough time with an infected individual to be at risk.
our approach can reliably detect subjects who have been in close proximity to an index case for a long enough time to be at risk.
we have shown that BLE data can provide a valuable source of information for epidemiological purposes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our proposed machine learning model is able to detect the risk of infection with an average accuracy of 90.3% for a false positive rate of 10%.
we can detect the risk of infection in the population with a high degree of accuracy and precision.
the BLE data collected from a large number of subjects is sufficient for the detection of subjects at risk of infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple machine learning model trained on a few thousand data points from a single day of measurements can reliably predict which subjects are at risk of being exposed to SARS-CoV-2.
a simple machine learning approach can reliably detect subjects at risk of infection with an accuracy of over 95%.
BLE data can be used to estimate the risk of SARS Co V 2 transmission with a reasonable accuracy.
